formulations.note: LABEL MISMATCH: the clinic list names this product as atenolol + bendroflumethiazide, but the UK product sold under the clinic's trade name contains atenolol + chlortalidone (a thiazide-like diuretic). No UK atenolol + bendroflumethiazide combination exists (emc and MHRA Products searched; the only UK bendroflumethiazide combination is with timolol). Everything shown here is for atenolol/chlortalidone. Confirm the pack contents with the clinic; if the clinic product really contains bendroflumethiazide, this information does not apply to it.

items.t: Management of hypertension (the 50 mg/12.5 mg strength: particularly suited to older patients).

src.q: 4.1 Therapeutic indications Management of hypertension.
The management of hypertension, particularly suited to older patients.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions stated in the UK SmPCs.

items.t: One tablet daily. Little or no further fall in blood pressure with higher doses; add another antihypertensive (e.g. a vasodilator) if needed.

src.q: Adults One tablet daily.
There is little or no further fall in blood pressure with increased dosage and, where necessary, another antihypertensive drug, such as a vasodilator, can be added.

items.t: One tablet daily (adults and elderly). If blood pressure is not controlled, a small dose of a third agent (e.g. a vasodilator) may be added.

src.q: Adults One tablet daily. Elderly One tablet daily.
Where hypertensive control is not achieved, addition of a small dose of a third agent e.g. as a vasodilator, may be appropriate.

items.t: Elderly: dose requirements are often lower; older patients not controlled on low-dose single-agent therapy should respond to one 50 mg/12.5 mg tablet daily.

src.q: Elderly Dosage requirements are often lower in this age group.
The elderly with hypertension who do not respond to low dose therapy with a single agent should have a satisfactory response to a single tablet daily of Tenoret.

items.t: Not recommended in children; safety and efficacy not established.

src.q: The use of Tenoretic is not recommended in children. The safety and efficacy of Tenoretic in children has not yet been established.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to atenolol, chlortalidone (or sulphonamide-derived medicines) or excipients; bradycardia; cardiogenic shock; hypotension; metabolic acidosis; severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbances; second- or third-degree heart block; sick sinus syndrome; untreated phaeochromocytoma; severe renal failure; uncontrolled heart failure; pregnancy; lactation.

src.q: hypersensitivity to the active substances (or to sulphonamide derived medicinal products) or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1

- bradycardia; - cardiogenic shock; - hypotension; - metabolic acidosis; - severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbances; - second- or third-degree heart block; - sick sinus syndrome; - untreated phaeochromocytoma; - severe renal failure; - uncontrolled heart failure.
Tenoretic tablets must not be given during pregnancy or lactation.

items.t: Heart failure: may be used once signs are controlled; caution with poor cardiac reserve. Do not stop abruptly in ischaemic heart disease. First-degree heart block: caution. Prinzmetal's angina: utmost caution.

src.q: may be used in patients whose signs of heart failure have been controlled. Caution must be exercised in patients whose cardiac reserve is poor.
should not be discontinued abruptly in patients suffering from ischaemic heart disease.
caution must be exercised if it is given to patients with first-degree heart block.

items.t: Bronchospastic disease (asthma): should in general not receive beta-blockers; if used, lowest dose with utmost caution; stop if airway resistance rises.

src.q: patients with bronchospastic disease should, in general, not receive beta-blockers due to increasing in airways resistance.
If increased airways resistance does occur, Tenoretic tablets should be discontinued and bronchodilator therapy (e.g. salbutamol) administered if necessary.

items.t: May mask hypoglycaemia warning signs (tachycardia, palpitations, sweating) and thyrotoxicosis signs; impaired glucose tolerance - monitor glycaemia closely early on.

src.q: may modify warning signs of hypoglycaemia as tachycardia, palpitation and sweating.
Close monitoring of glycaemia is recommended in the initial phase of therapy

items.t: Electrolytes: hypokalaemia and hyponatraemia may occur; check electrolytes periodically, especially in the elderly, those on digitalis, on low-potassium diets or with GI complaints.

src.q: plasma electrolyte should be periodically determined in appropriate intervals to detect possible electrolyte imbalance especially hypokalaemia and hyponatraemia.

items.t: Phaeochromocytoma: give only after alpha-blockade. Anaesthesia: inform the anaesthetist. History of anaphylaxis: reactions may be more severe and less responsive to adrenaline.

src.q: in patients with phaeochromocytoma must be administered only after alfa-receptor blockade.
Such patients may be unresponsive to the usual doses of adrenaline used to treat the allergic reactions.

items.t: Impaired hepatic function or progressive liver disease: minor fluid/electrolyte changes may precipitate hepatic coma. Hyperuricaemia may occur. Choroidal effusion/acute angle-closure glaucoma: stop as rapidly as possible.

src.q: in patients with impaired hepatic function or progressive liver disease, minor alterations in fluid and electrolyte balance may precipitate hepatic coma.
The primary treatment is to discontinue drug intake as rapidly as possible.

items.t: Verapamil or diltiazem: exaggerated negative effects (severe hypotension, bradycardia, cardiac failure), especially with impaired ventricular function or conduction problems; do not give either intravenously within 48 hours of stopping the other.

src.q: This may result in severe hypotension, bradycardia and cardiac failure.
Neither the beta-blocker nor the calcium channel blocker should be administered intravenously within 48 hours of discontinuing the other.

items.t: Dihydropyridines (e.g. nifedipine): more hypotension; cardiac failure possible with latent cardiac insufficiency.

src.q: Concomitant therapy with dihydropyridines e.g. nifedipine, may increase the risk of hypotension, and cardiac failure may occur in patients with latent cardiac insufficiency.

items.t: Insulin and oral antidiabetics: blood-sugar-lowering effects may be intensified (and hypoglycaemia warning signs masked).

src.q: Concomitant use with insulin and oral antidiabetic drugs may lead to the intensification of the blood sugar lowering effects of these drugs.

items.t: NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen) may reduce the antihypertensive effect. Sympathomimetics (e.g. adrenaline) may counteract the beta-blocker.

src.q: Concomitant use of prostaglandin synthetase inhibiting drugs (e.g. ibuprofen, indometacin) may decrease the hypotensive effects of beta-blockers
Concomitant use of sympathomimetic agents, e.g. adrenaline (epinephrine), may counteract the effect of beta-blockers.

items.t: Lithium: renal clearance reduced (dose adjustment may be needed). Clonidine: withdraw the beta-blocker several days before stopping clonidine. Digitalis, class I antiarrhythmics and amiodarone: conduction effects.

src.q: The chlortalidone component may reduce the renal clearance of lithium leading to increased serum concentrations.
If the two drugs are co-administered, the beta-blocker should be withdrawn several days before discontinuing clonidine.

items.t: Contraindicated in severe renal failure (no CrCl/eGFR threshold given). Reduced efficacy in renal insufficiency because of the chlortalidone component.

src.q: This fixed dose combination should thus not be administrated to patients with severe renal impairment
Due to the properties of the chlortalidone component, Tenoretic tablets has reduced efficacy in the presence of renal insufficiency.

items.t: Impaired hepatic function or progressive liver disease: minor fluid and electrolyte changes may precipitate hepatic coma.

src.q: in patients with impaired hepatic function or progressive liver disease, minor alterations in fluid and electrolyte balance may precipitate hepatic coma.

items.t: SmPC: must not be given during pregnancy (section 4.3).

src.q: Pregnancy: Tenoretic tablets must not be given during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS (atenolol alone, not the combination): can be used in pregnancy if recommended by a doctor; may be linked with a smaller baby. BUMPS (diuretics in general): diuretics may reduce placental blood flow, and the baby will be monitored with extra growth scans. This differs from the combination SmPC, which says must not be given.

src.q: Atenolol can be used in pregnancy if recommended by a doctor.
Women taking atenolol may be more likely to have a smaller baby.
Diuretics may reduce blood flow to the placenta.
Your baby will be monitored with extra growth scans.

items.t: SmPC: must not be given during lactation (section 4.3).

src.q: Lactation: Tenoretic tablets must not be given during lactation.

items.t: SPS (atenolol alone): use with caution; labetalol, metoprolol or propranolol preferred. Risk of accumulation in neonates; monitor the infant for bradycardia and hypoglycaemia (drowsiness, lethargy, poor feeding).

src.q: It can be used with caution during breastfeeding, but labetalol, metoprolol, or propranolol are preferred if clinically appropriate.
Monitor infants for signs of bradycardia or hypoglycaemia including drowsiness, lethargy, and poor feeding and inadequate weight gain.

items.t: No fertility data available.

src.q: Fertility: No data on fertility available.

items.t: Common: bradycardia, cold extremities, gastrointestinal disturbance (including nausea), fatigue; and, from chlortalidone, hyperuricaemia, hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia, impaired glucose tolerance.

src.q: Cardiac disorders Common Bradycardia
Vascular disorders Common Cold extremities
Common Related to chlortalidone: Hyperuricaemia, hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia, impaired glucose tolerance

items.t: Rare: worsening heart failure, precipitation of heart block, bronchospasm in asthma, purpura/thrombocytopenia/leucopenia, hepatic toxicity including intrahepatic cholestasis, pancreatitis. Not known: choroidal effusion, hypersensitivity reactions including angioedema and urticaria.

src.q: Rare Heart failure deterioration, precipitation of heart block
Rare Bronchospasm may occur in patients with bronchial asthma or a history of asthmatic complaints
Rare Purpura, thrombocytopenia, leucopenia (related to chlortalidone)
Rare Hepatic toxicity including intrahepatic cholestasis, pancreatitis (related to chlortalidone)
Not known Hypersensitivity reactions, including angioedema and urticaria

items.t: Choroidal effusion, acute myopia and acute angle-closure glaucoma (sulfonamide-type reaction): sudden reduced vision or eye pain, usually within hours to weeks of starting. Stop the medicine as rapidly as possible; untreated angle-closure glaucoma can cause permanent vision loss.

src.q: Symptoms include acute onset of decreased visual acuity or ocular pain and typically occur within hours to weeks of drug initiation.
Untreated acute angle-closure glaucoma can lead to permanent vision loss.
The primary treatment is to discontinue drug intake as rapidly as possible.

items.t: Plasma electrolytes periodically (hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia); blood glucose closely at the start in diabetes and periodic glucosuria tests in prolonged therapy.

src.q: plasma electrolyte should be periodically determined in appropriate intervals to detect possible electrolyte imbalance especially hypokalaemia and hyponatraemia.
in prolonged therapy test for glucosuria should be carried out at regular intervals.

items.t: Stop if airway resistance increases. If slow heart rate causes symptoms, the dose may be reduced. Consider stopping if wellbeing is adversely affected by adverse reactions.

src.q: In the rare instances when a treated patient develops symptoms which may be attributable to a slow heart rate, the dose may be reduced.
Discontinuance of Tenoretic tablets should be considered if, according to clinical judgement, the well-being of the patient is adversely affected by any of the above reactions.

items.t: Oral, once daily. The score line is not for breaking the tablet.

src.q: The score line is not intended for breaking the tablet.

items.t: Do not stop suddenly (especially with heart disease). If you have ever had asthma or wheezing, check with your doctor before taking.

src.q: If you have ever had asthma or wheezing, do not take this medicine without first checking with your doctor

items.t: Occasional dizziness or fatigue may affect driving.

src.q: it should be taken into account that occasionally dizziness or fatigue may occur.
